title: The Cheapest Crew of K Workers

concept.title: Within a crew everyone is paid at the same rate per unit of quality, and that rate is set by the worker with the highest wage-to-quality ratio
body: A factory must hire **exactly `k` workers**. The worker `i` has a *quality* `q[i]` and demands a *minimum wage* `w[i]`. The pay rules are: every worker of the crew is paid **in proportion to quality** (so the pay of the worker `i` is `q[i] * rate` for the same `rate` for the whole crew), and nobody is paid less than the minimum wage. What is the **smallest total pay**? Print it **rounded up to a whole number**. For the qualities `10 20 5`, the wages `70 50 30` and `k = 2` the answer is 105: hire the workers 1 and 3 at the rate 7 per unit of quality, which pays 70 and 35.

For a fixed crew the rate must satisfy `rate >= w[i] / q[i]` for **every member**, so the smallest rate is the **largest ratio `w/q`** among the members, and the total pay is `rate * (sum of the qualities)`. Now think of the crew's *bottleneck* worker, the one with the largest ratio. Sort all workers by the ratio `w/q`. When the worker `i` of this order is the bottleneck, the crew can be formed from any workers **before him in the order** (their ratios are not higher), and to make the total pay small we take the `k - 1` of them with the **smallest qualities**, together with `i`.

The heap keeps the `k` smallest qualities seen so far, and each worker is the bottleneck candidate once. The payment is a fraction, so the program compares candidates by **cross-multiplication** (exact integers, no floating point); the ratio comparison used for sorting is exact in the same way. With the limits above every product stays below 10^17. The total time is O(n log n).

statement: A crew of exactly `k` workers must be hired. The worker `i` has the quality `q[i]` and the minimum wage `w[i]`. All the crew members are paid in the same proportion to their quality, nobody receives less than his minimum wage, and the total pay must be as small as possible. Print the smallest total pay rounded up to the next whole number.
inputFormat: The first line has `n` and `k`: the number of workers and the size of the crew.
The second line has `n` numbers: the quality of each worker.
The third line has `n` numbers: the minimum wage of each worker.
outputFormat: Print the smallest total pay, rounded up.

examples.note: The ratios wage/quality are 7, 2.5 and 6. The workers 1 and 3 at the rate 7 are paid 70 and 35: 105 (the workers 2 and 3 at the rate 6 would cost 150).

hints: For a crew, the rate is the largest w/q among its members.
Sort the workers by w/q; the current worker is the largest ratio of the crew.
Keep the k smallest qualities in a max-heap and use exact fraction comparison.

explanation: The workers are sorted by the ratio wage/quality; for each worker as the bottleneck the k smallest qualities seen so far are kept with a max-heap, the candidate payment is the quality sum times the bottleneck ratio (an exact fraction), and the smallest candidate rounded up is printed.
solution.complexity: Time O(n log n), space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

from heapq import heappush, heappop
from functools import cmp_to_key

n, k = map(int, input().split())
q = list(map(int, input().split()))
w = list(map(int, input().split()))

order = sorted(range(n), key=cmp_to_key(lambda i, j: w[i] * q[j] - w[j] * q[i]))
heap = []
sumq = 0
bn, bd = -1, 1
for i in order:
    heappush(heap, -q[i])
    sumq += q[i]
    if len(heap) > k:
        sumq += heappop(heap)
    if len(heap) == k:
        num = sumq * w[i]
        den = q[i]
        if bn < 0 or num * bd < bn * den:
            bn, bd = num, den
print((bn + bd - 1) // bd)
